added.long_description:
Spacecraft today have to generate all their own power, which caps what can be built and operated in orbit. Central Blue is building the power grid for space: satellites that collect sunlight and beam power by laser to receiver panels on other spacecraft.

Our first power-beaming prototype is nearly complete in Seattle, with a laser-powered propulsion demonstration planned with Wave Motion Launch Technologies. Our CORE software will let the power satellites detect faults and recover on their own, keeping the grid running around the clock.

long_description.before:
Expanse unlocks wasted GPU capacity. We recover idle compute through three capabilities: resource prediction (right-sizing job submissions before they reach the scheduler), optimisation suggestions (code and config changes researchers can apply themselves), and failure prediction (catching jobs that will fail before they consume hours of GPU time).

We’re four engineers. We ran HPC and GPU training workloads at the largest quant funds and national supercomputing centres. We faced this problem first hand and the only fix was to over-provision and burn millions. Ismaeel built the first multimodal HPC resource predictor as research at EPCC (Edinburgh’s Parallel Computing Centre), which beat every published baseline. This is the tool we wish we had.
long_description.after:
Expanse delivers compute certainty. Its software predicts exactly what every AI workload needs before it runs, so organisations can do more with the GPU infrastructure they already own, privately and on their own hardware.

Every AI breakthrough begins with a compute decision, and today that decision is a guess. Ask for too little and the job dies hours in. Ask for too much and the hardware sits reserved and idle while other work waits. Expanse replaces the guess with evidence, before a single GPU is committed.

We're four engineers who ran and managed GPU clusters at some of the world's largest quantitative hedge funds, following earlier research at national supercomputing scale. This was the tool we always wanted, so we built it.

one_liner.after: Twice the work from the GPUs you already own

long_description.before:
Production AI agents keep making the same mistakes. The usual fix is another line in the system prompt. Over time, the agent carries instructions for dozens of situations, even when it’s doing something simple, and every correction becomes another thing to maintain.

Mirrors lets developers maintain production agents by turning recurring mistakes into targeted corrections. It surfaces recurring mistakes across production runs. Developers write a correction, choose the situations where it applies, and preview its scope against past conversations. Once activated, Mirrors adds the correction to the agent only in those situations. Developers can then compare outcomes with and without the correction to see whether it helps. Unlike skills, the agent doesn’t decide what to load. The scope developers set does.

Corrections live in one place, scoped to the right accounts and workflows. Mirrors connects through an SDK and works with any agent framework. The application keeps control of its model calls and tools.
long_description.after: Mirrors gives developers the infrastructure to control what production AI agents are told, and when. Today that lives in long prompts and skills the agent may never open, so agents keep breaking rules they've already been given. With Mirrors, a developer writes a rule once and defines where it applies, and Mirrors delivers it at that step of the run and measures whether it helped. It works with any agent framework and any model. As agents take on more of a company's work, what they're told becomes how the company runs.

one_liner.before: Fix recurring AI agent mistakes with real-time guidance
one_liner.after: The guidance system for production AI agents

Staging environments and test sandboxes don't scale for development with AI.

Rystic is building the verification layer for software written by AI. We give every change a deterministic simulated environment, populated with local, stateful simulators of APIs like Slack, Stripe, GitHub, and PostHog. Control everything about your dependencies, from the clock to injected faults, and use our harness for integration tests or agent evals.

long_description.before:
Sutrix turns messy data from EHRs, clinical notes, wearables, and surveys into clean, study-ready datasets allowing healthcare research teams to deliver tailored patient care faster.

Before a clinical study can start, research staff spend weeks pulling patient data from disconnected systems like the EHR, REDCap, and wearable platforms, reading notes chart by chart, and reconciling conflicting entries in spreadsheets. Sutrix automates that work by deploying AI systems within each team’s own environment, linking patient records across sources, applying the study's rules, and flagging unclear cases for staff to review.

Paying research teams at 10+ institutions cut data prep by 80% going from months per study to weeks.

We're brothers who've built together for 4 years. We first solved this problem doing forward-deployed work at HSS, where we built an injury surveillance system now used by 700+ teams. Ritvik's clinical research at HSS and Emory showed us every research team has the same bottleneck. Supratik previously founded Kairo (a16z Speedrun, exited) and built production AI agents at Amazon.

long_description.before:
Vibe Robotics builds robots for the work nobody should have to repeat.

Every day in every hotel, towels go up to rooms, linens move between floors, and stacks of laundry need to be folded before the next guests arrive. It’s hard, physical, and hotels can’t hire enough people to do it.

Vibe 01 is built for exactly that. It carries, delivers and folds. Two arms, a lift column, and a camera head on a base that drives itself through back-of-house hallways and service elevators. It learns by watching people do the job, then does it on its own. Vibe 01 can already fold a towel fully autonomously in 23.8 seconds, a skill it learned from just a few hundred human demonstrations.

We’re Archer, Daniel, Katherine and Pranav. We’re starting in hotels and building toward everywhere people work.
long_description.after:
Vibe Robotics builds robots for the work nobody should have to repeat.

We’re starting in hotels. Every day, housekeeping teams move linens between floors, restock carts, and fold stacks of laundry before the next guests arrive. It’s physical work that has to get done every shift.

Our first robot, Vibe 01, folds a hand towel fully autonomously in 23.8 seconds. It learned from just a few hundred human demonstrations. We’re piloting Vibe 01 at a Hilton property and working with hotels under the Marriott, Hilton, and IHG brands to bring it to more locations.

Folding is the first job. Next are restocking housekeeping carts and moving linens between floors. We’re Archer, Daniel, Katherine, and Pranav, and we’re building robots that can learn to do routine physical work across industries.
